review.method: Explicit coding-assistant lexical/constituent review of exact N1904 Greek and displayed LSV. Inflection, syntax, repetition and witness differences checked; pending independent peer and reader review. No raw LSV Strong-tag or inferred global lexical assignments.
review.sourceTokenization: Explicit zero-based whitespace tokens including punctuation.

1:1.sourceText: Παῦλος δοῦλος Θεοῦ, ἀπόστολος δὲ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ κατὰ πίστιν ἐκλεκτῶν Θεοῦ καὶ ἐπίγνωσιν ἀληθείας τῆς κατ’ εὐσέβειαν
1:1.targetText: Paul, a servant of God, and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of the chosen ones of God, and an acknowledging of truth that [is] according to piety,

unmappedTarget.reason: English copula supplied in a Greek verbless clause; no corresponding finite Greek verb.

1:2.sourceText: ἐπ’ ἐλπίδι ζωῆς αἰωνίου, ἣν ἐπηγγείλατο ὁ ἀψευδὴς Θεὸς πρὸ χρόνων αἰωνίων,
1:2.targetText: on hope of continuous life, which God, who does not lie, promised before times of ages

groups.note: The adjective ἀψευδής means truthful/not lying; English recasts it as does not lie in a relative modifier. No separate Greek finite lying verb is invented.
The adjective αἰωνίων qualifies times as age-long/eternal; LSV recasts the modifier as of ages, without an extra separate Greek ages noun.

1:3.sourceText: ἐφανέρωσεν δὲ καιροῖς ἰδίοις τὸν λόγον αὐτοῦ ἐν κηρύγματι ὃ ἐπιστεύθην ἐγὼ κατ’ ἐπιταγὴν τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Θεοῦ,
1:3.targetText: (and He revealed His word in [His] own times), in preaching, which I was entrusted with, according to a charge of God our Savior,

groups.note: The own adjective ἰδίοις qualifies the times belonging to the acting God; English makes that possessor explicit as bracketed His own. There is no additional printed Greek His pronoun at this times modifier.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:4.sourceText: Τίτῳ γνησίῳ τέκνῳ κατὰ κοινὴν πίστιν· χάρις καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς καὶ Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν.
1:4.targetText: to Titus—true child according to a common faith: Grace, [[kindness,]] peace, from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior!

unmappedSource.reason: N1904 explicitly coordinates grace and peace with καί; LSV lists grace, bracketed kindness, peace without a separate and between these items. The later and with Father has its own actual καί.
The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness noun addition: LSV double-bracketed kindness follows TR ἔλεος, absent from pinned N1904 grace and peace.
Source-witness title addition: LSV the Lord follows TR κυρίου before Jesus Christ; N1904 has Christ Jesus without the Lord title.

review.note: The Jesus/Christ order reverses N1904 Christ Jesus; each actual name/title is preserved separately.

1:5.sourceText: Τούτου χάριν ἀπέλιπόν σε ἐν Κρήτῃ ἵνα τὰ λείποντα ἐπιδιορθώσῃ, καὶ καταστήσῃς κατὰ πόλιν πρεσβυτέρους, ὡς ἐγώ σοι διεταξάμην,
1:5.targetText: For this cause I left you in Crete, that you may arrange the things lacking, and may set elders down in every city, as I appointed to you,

groups.note: The genitive demonstrative plus χάριν construction means for the sake of this; English for this cause renders that complete causal expression without inventing a separate Greek cause noun.
The distributive κατά with city means city by city/in each city; English in every expresses that distributive relation without a separate Greek every adjective.

1:6.sourceText: εἴ τίς ἐστιν ἀνέγκλητος, μιᾶς γυναικὸς ἀνήρ, τέκνα ἔχων πιστά, μὴ ἐν κατηγορίᾳ ἀσωτίας ἢ ἀνυπότακτα.
1:6.targetText: if anyone is blameless, a husband of one wife, having believing children, not under accusation of riotous living or insubordinate—

groups.note: Greek ἐν with accusation means in/under an accusation; English under states that accusatory status, not a claim that ἐν generally means under.

1:7.sourceText: δεῖ γὰρ τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ἀνέγκλητον εἶναι ὡς Θεοῦ οἰκονόμον, μὴ αὐθάδη, μὴ ὀργίλον, μὴ πάροινον, μὴ πλήκτην, μὴ αἰσχροκερδῆ,
1:7.targetText: for it is required of the overseer to be blameless, as God’s steward, not self-pleased, nor prone to anger, not given to wine, not an abuser, not given to shameful gain,

groups.note: The repeated Greek μή in the negative trait list is rendered nor for this item, preserving the negative coordination without a separately written οὐδέ.

1:8.sourceText: ἀλλὰ φιλόξενον, φιλάγαθον, σώφρονα, δίκαιον, ὅσιον, ἐγκρατῆ,
1:8.targetText: but a lover of strangers, a lover of [the] good, sober-minded, righteous, holy, self-controlled,

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English article identifies the good in the good-loving compound; Greek φιλἀγαθον is one adjective without a separate article token.

1:9.sourceText: ἀντεχόμενον τοῦ κατὰ τὴν διδαχὴν πιστοῦ λόγου, ἵνα δυνατὸς ᾖ καὶ παρακαλεῖν ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ τῇ ὑγιαινούσῃ καὶ τοὺς ἀντιλέγοντας ἐλέγχειν.
1:9.targetText: holding—according to the teaching—to the steadfast word, that he may also be able to exhort in the sound teaching, and to convict the deniers;

groups.note: The substantival speaking-against participle ἀντιλέγοντας designates people contradicting; LSV renders deniers, not an invented separate denial noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:10.sourceText: Εἰσὶν γὰρ πολλοὶ ἀνυπότακτοι, ματαιολόγοι καὶ φρεναπάται, μάλιστα οἱ ἐκ τῆς περιτομῆς,
1:10.targetText: for there are many both insubordinate, vain-talkers, and mind-deceivers—especially those of the circumcision—

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds both to introduce the coordinated descriptions; N1904 has no corresponding extra additive particle before insubordinate.

1:11.sourceText: οὓς δεῖ ἐπιστομίζειν, οἵτινες ὅλους οἴκους ἀνατρέπουσιν διδάσκοντες ἃ μὴ δεῖ αἰσχροῦ κέρδους χάριν.
1:11.targetText: whose mouths must be covered, who overturn whole households, teaching what things it should not, for [the] sake of shameful gain.

groups.note: The mouth-stopping verb ἐπιστομίζειν means silence/stop the mouth; LSV expands it into mouths ... be covered. The relative people-object is thereby recast as whose, a possessor of the mouths implicit in that compound, without a separate Greek mouth noun.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English article completes the for-the-sake-of idiom; the Greek postposition χάριν contains no separate definite article.

1:12.sourceText: εἶπέν τις ἐξ αὐτῶν ἴδιος αὐτῶν προφήτης Κρῆτες ἀεὶ ψεῦσται, κακὰ θηρία, γαστέρες ἀργαί.
1:12.targetText: A certain one of them, a prophet of their own, said, “Cretans! Always liars, evil beasts, lazy bellies!”

1:13.sourceText: ἡ μαρτυρία αὕτη ἐστὶν ἀληθής. δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν ἔλεγχε αὐτοὺς ἀποτόμως, ἵνα ὑγιαίνωσιν ἐν τῇ πίστει,
1:13.targetText: This testimony is true; for which cause convict them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article has no separate English article in this noun phrase; the English noun, modifier, or coordination expresses its reference.

1:14.sourceText: μὴ προσέχοντες Ἰουδαϊκοῖς μύθοις καὶ ἐντολαῖς ἀνθρώπων ἀποστρεφομένων τὴν ἀλήθειαν.
1:14.targetText: not giving heed to Jewish fables and commands of men, turning themselves away from the truth.

groups.note: The middle turning-away participle describes the command-giving men rejecting truth; LSV explicitly renders themselves in its middle-voice predicate without an independent reflexive source pronoun.

1:15.sourceText: πάντα καθαρὰ τοῖς καθαροῖς· τοῖς δὲ μεμιαμμένοις καὶ ἀπίστοις οὐδὲν καθαρόν, ἀλλὰ μεμίανται αὐτῶν καὶ ὁ νοῦς καὶ ἡ συνείδησις.
1:15.targetText: All things, indeed, [are] pure to the pure, and nothing [is] pure to the defiled and unsteadfast, but even the mind and the conscience of them [is] defiled.

groups.note: The dative article with the coordinated defiled/unbelieving designation supplies the case-marked recipient relation to the; both subsequent descriptions share that written dative phrase.
The actual perfect passive μεμίανται means has been defiled; it supports the final English bracketed is plus defiled. These brackets do not erase the genuine written defiling predicate.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness particle addition: LSV indeed follows TR μέν, absent from pinned N1904.

1:16.sourceText: Θεὸν ὁμολογοῦσιν εἰδέναι, τοῖς δὲ ἔργοις ἀρνοῦνται, βδελυκτοὶ ὄντες καὶ ἀπειθεῖς καὶ πρὸς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθὸν ἀδόκιμοι.
1:16.targetText: They profess to know God, but they deny [Him] by their works, being abominable, and disobedient, and disapproved to every good work.

groups.note: The one fronted God object is what they profess to know and the understood object of the contrasted denying predicate; English repeats that same object as bracketed Him. Both preserve the actual God identity without inventing another source pronoun.

The instrumental dative article/works phrase identifies the professing people’s conduct; English renders by their works. Their is the contextual possessive in that complete case-marked noun phrase, not an extra Greek pronoun assigned to the article alone.
